title: Resume and checkpoint across hybrid CPU+GPU path
description:
## Goal

Drain semantics for in-flight GPU batches at SIGINT or
heartbeat-checkpoint boundary; resume from checkpoint produces
byte-identical deterministic columns vs an uninterrupted reference
run. Builds on `5f12e7ff` (CPU-only heartbeat) by adding the GPU
drain protocol from design doc §4.

## Context

Task under story `9e853c62` (Hybrid CPU+GPU executor) within epic
`gf2-sim` (`f9717e7e`). Phase 0 design doc:
`dev/active/ec530af9-pipeline-design.md` §4 (heartbeat schema v2 +
drain protocol). Wave C.2 fan-out from `75c22fa8`.

**AMENDMENT 2026-06-10 (user-approved; alignment to the landed C.1
scheduler — no rigor change).** The original deliverable-3 said the
scheduler "restores each worker's ChaCha20Rng to the recorded
`rng_word_pos`", anticipating design §4's per-worker-RNG-stream
fixed-partition executor. The landed, reviewed C.1 scheduler
(`75c22fa8`) instead keys EVERY frame's randomness on the global
frame index (`worker_offset(seed, snr_idx, 0, g)`, the §3
logical-worker-0 convention) and distributes work in strided
partitions — exactly what preserves `3fcb7025`'s cross-worker-count
byte-identity. Resume therefore restores per-worker PROGRESS
(`frames_in_worker`) and folds the saved counters; per-frame RNG
positions are re-derived from the global frame index, and
`rng_word_pos` stays RECORDED per the v2 schema but is not read
back. Design §4 was corrected in the same amendment. Criterion-2 was
tightened to name the HYBRID-executor reference path and the
same-host test scope (single gfx1030 in CI; cross-host portability
is documented, not asserted). The 4-column byte-identity assertion
is unchanged and stays [hard].

## Deliverables

1. `crates/gf2-sim/src/executor/drain.rs`:
   - `Scheduler::drain_for_checkpoint()` invoking
     `hipStreamSynchronize()` on each owned stream (NOT
     `hipDeviceSynchronize()`, per design-doc §4 note: avoid
     blocking other contexts).
   - Per-stream "in-flight batches" tally so the drain knows when
     every stream is idle.
2. Integration with `gf2-sim::checkpoint::CheckpointWriter`
   (`5f12e7ff`):
   - At heartbeat boundary, scheduler calls `drain_for_checkpoint`
     before the writer serialises.
   - Per-worker `frames_in_worker` (and the §4-formula
     `rng_word_pos`, recorded for schema fidelity) captured AFTER
     the drain (so the resume offset is correct).
3. Resume protocol (amended 2026-06-10, see AMENDMENT above):
   - On `--resume`, the scheduler reads `worker_states[]` from the
     v2 checkpoint and restores each worker's strided-partition
     PROGRESS from `frames_in_worker`, folding the saved counters.
   - Per-frame RNG positions are re-derived from the global frame
     index exactly as in an uninterrupted run (§3 logical-worker-0
     keying); `rng_word_pos` is recorded but not read back.
   - First batch after resume processes the same global frame
     indices, with the same per-frame RNG offsets, that the
     uninterrupted run would have processed next.
4. Hybrid resume parity test in
   `crates/gf2-sim/tests/hybrid_resume.rs` (under `--features hip`):
   - SIGINT during a 10-SNR sweep with GPU stages active at frame
     N.
   - Resume produces byte-identical
     `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters` vs an uninterrupted
     HYBRID-executor reference at the same seed and worker count
     for 3 (rate, modulation) configurations.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] SIGINT during hybrid execution drains in-flight GPU batches
  before flushing the v2 checkpoint per design-doc §4.
- [hard] Resume from that checkpoint on the same host (single-gfx1030
  CI; cross-host portability is documented, not asserted) produces
  byte-identical `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters` vs an
  uninterrupted HYBRID-executor reference run at the same seed and
  worker count for the 3 named DVB-T2 configurations. (`mean_iters`
  is INCLUDED: resume-vs-uninterrupted is a same-path comparison, so
  the §11 CPU-vs-GPU exclusion does not apply.)
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- CPU-only heartbeat (owned by `5f12e7ff`).
- Failure-mode wiring (owned by `42eac5cc`).
- Cross-host resume verification (no second host in CI; the v2
  checkpoint format itself is host-independent JSON).
